source.fonts: src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx (next/font: Heebo, Frank Ruhl Libre, Noto Sans Arabic per ar, Noto Sans per ru)

background.purpose: The page: the building's cladding, warm not grey.

foreground.purpose: Text, the aisle numerals, the ghost button.

chrome.purpose: The header bar: the flag's blue field.

on-chrome.purpose: Text and the stripe on the chrome.

chrome-hover.purpose: Hover veil under icon buttons, the language select and the active mobile item.

surface.purpose: Cards, tables, the float menu, the search dais, form controls.

surface-sunken.purpose: Table headers, unselected toggles, the meter track, ghost and menu-item hover. Lighter than the card in dark mode: depth cues invert there.

surface-hover.purpose: Hover of a ruled row, a table row, an interactive card.

line.purpose: Every card border and every rule between rows and sections.

line-strong.purpose: Form controls, the search dais, an interactive card's hover border.

muted.purpose: Secondary text, captions, the source-and-date line, placeholders. At least 6:1 on every light surface.

accent.purpose: FILL: primary actions, selected toggles, the seat, the meter, selection, the caret.

accent-ink.purpose: TEXT: links, view-all, the active menu item, the leading stat. Diverges from the fill in dark mode.

accent-soft.purpose: Secondary button hover, the accent badge.

accent-deep.purpose: Primary button and search-submit hover. Legacy alias; becomes a hover token in Stage D.

coalition.purpose: Seat fill and stroke, the hollow-seat glyph, the coalition meter. Same value as opposition by design.

opposition.purpose: The opposition meter. Same value as coalition by design: the aisle carries the split.

pass.purpose: Fill: a passed vote's meter or bar.

pass-soft.purpose: Badge background for a passed vote.

fail.purpose: Fill: a failed vote's meter or bar. A result, never a bloc.

fail-soft.purpose: Badge background for a rejected vote.

warn-soft.purpose: Badge background: a former member, an unconfirmed date.

info.purpose: The informational tone: the blue family under the status naming.

focus.purpose: The inner halo of the focus ring. Never text.

focus-ring.purpose: The outer 3px outline of the focus ring: ink in light, white in dark. Guarantees 3:1 on any surface.

display.purpose: The page title, one per page (h1). 2.25rem, rising to 3rem with line-height 1 from 640px. Frank Ruhl Libre.

wordmark.purpose: The site name in the chrome with the flag inside its letters (.wordmark: inline-SVG stripes and star clipped to the glyphs, white stroke, plain-white fallback). Frank Ruhl Libre.

figure.purpose: The one number a ruled row leads with. Frank Ruhl Libre, tabular. The aisle numerals are the same voice drawn inside the hall's SVG (font-size 14 viewBox units in the arc, 13 in the phone blocks) and scale with the drawing.

headline.purpose: Section headings (h2): SectionHeading variant lg. Heebo.

title.purpose: Sub-block and 'now'-column headings: SectionHeading variant md. Heebo.

body.purpose: Prose and the page's base size.

body-small.purpose: The working size: lists, tables, nav links, form controls.

label.purpose: Field labels, toggles, small buttons, a member's name in a row.

caption.purpose: The source-and-date line, hints, timestamps, table captions, last-sync. Always muted.

micro.purpose: The 'automatic translation' mark; declared as --text-micro (0.6875rem / 1rem line), never text-[11px].

stat.purpose: The Stat primitive's headline figure. Heebo, not the serif: a stat is a fact, a figure in a ruled row is a finding.

fonts.name: Frank Ruhl Libre
fonts.role: display: wordmark, page title, aisle numerals, finding figures

fonts.name: Noto Sans Arabic
fonts.role: body face first in :lang(ar); display fallback

fonts.name: Noto Sans
fonts.role: body face first in :lang(ru); display fallback

shadows.name: shadow-float
shadows.purpose: The only shadow: things that float over content (the More menu, the mobile nav panel). Tinted to ink, hairline built in. Never on cards, tables, the search dais or the header.

shadows.name: stripe-rule
shadows.purpose: The flag's two stripes as the rule beneath the chrome; a rule, not an elevation.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.purpose: Every hover in the system is a colour change at Tailwind's default duration; nothing lifts, scales or slides.

motion.name: seat
motion.purpose: A seat lighting or dimming when a faction is hovered or focused in the legend.

motion.name: skip-link
motion.purpose: The skip link sliding in on focus.

motion.name: a11y-no-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation and transition must survive being zeroed.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: The hall changes form (two blocks → the arc); the latest-votes list becomes a table; the display title steps from 2.25rem to 3rem.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: The nav goes inline (seven links + More); findings become two columns.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The 'now' column moves beside the hall as a 19rem side column.

layout.container: 72rem (max-w-6xl), 1rem gutter, 2rem block padding; the header shares the container
layout.nowColumn: 19rem at ≥1024px, hairline on the start edge, 2.5rem inline padding, 3.5rem column gap; stacked beneath a top hairline with 2rem padding below
layout.ruledRow: 0.625rem block padding, 0.75rem gap, 36px avatar, hover extends 0.5rem past the text edge (-mx-2 px-2), chip radius
layout.tableCell: 0.5rem × 0.75rem; header row surface-sunken at 0.75rem/500 muted; numeric columns end-aligned tabular

focus.rule: :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 3px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--focus); border-radius: 2px; }
focus.purpose: An ink (light) or white (dark) outline OUTSIDE an amber halo. Amber alone is 1.65:1 on white; the outer ring guarantees ≥3:1 on any surface. html.a11y-keyboard replaces it with an accent double ring on :focus.

browserSurfaces.tapHighlight: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 18%, transparent); touch-action: manipulation on a, button, summary, [role=button]

accessibilityLayer.note: Classes the accessibility menu adds to <html>. A constraint the world respects, not a theme it designs for.
accessibilityLayer.a11y-contrast: Black page, white text and lines, #ffff00 accent and links, #8ab4ff for both blocs; the chrome goes black. Uses !important and beats every token.
accessibilityLayer.a11y-grayscale: filter: grayscale(100%) — nothing may depend on hue alone.
accessibilityLayer.a11y-links: Yellow marker (#fff2a8 / #b8860b ring) on links; outline on buttons.
accessibilityLayer.a11y-headings: accent outline and 8% tint on h1–h3.
accessibilityLayer.a11y-keyboard: accent double ring on any :focus; 6rem scroll-margin on focusables so they clear the sticky chrome.
accessibilityLayer.a11y-readable: Arial, 1.7 line-height, 0.02em spacing forced on everything (!important).
accessibilityLayer.a11y-no-motion: All animation and transition durations to 0s.
accessibilityLayer.text-scaling: font-size % on <html>; the whole UI is rem-based and scales with it.

enforcement.guards: Every @theme colour token is defined under :root, html.dark and html.a11y-contrast; listed text/surface pairs clear 4.5:1 (3:1 for accent-as-component and focus-ring) in every root; every semantic-looking class in src/ resolves to a declared token.
No physical left/right utilities, style props or CSS declarations in src/; SpectrumBar.tsx is the only allow-listed file.

Per-file ratchet on bg-white, black/white overlays, raw Tailwind palette hues and text-[11px]; budget in tests/qa/legacy-utilities.budget.json (301 across 41 files) may only decrease; a file without a budget may not add any.
Each ui/ primitive renders its static variant classes and ARIA (Card has no shadow; SectionHeading has no uppercase/tracking; Meter has role=meter; toggles emit aria-pressed).
No Hebrew literals in src/; every UI string in all four message files with identical keys and ICU placeholders.

transitional.note: Not the system. The class-name dark-mode retrofit block in globals.css (html.dark .bg-white {…} and raw-hue overrides) coexists with the token layer and is being ratcheted out; Stage D removes it and turns the ratchet into a ban.
notCanonized: SectionHeading variant="eyebrow" (text-sm font-semibold text-muted) is defined but unused; not a pattern to adopt
search/elections pages: h2/h3 with uppercase tracking-wide (pre-migration)

contractDivergences.contract: OWN-WORLD: 'a turned seat voted against its faction'
contractDivergences.built: Not built. Seat states are filled / hollow / lit / dimmed only.

contractDivergences.contract: FIRST VIEWPORT: 'coalition on the start side, opposition on the end side' (logical)
contractDivergences.built: Fixed physically: opposition LEFT of the aisle, coalition RIGHT, direction: ltr in every locale — matches the contract in RTL locales (he, ar) and mirrors it in LTR (en, ru), by the election-broadcast convention.

contractDivergences.contract: Unresolved: flag-filled lettering vs a flat wordmark beside a small flag
contractDivergences.built: Resolved at build, then revised on the user's call: flag-filled lettering, rebuilt as vector (fixed geometry per locale, real fallback) — the old raster's idea without its defects.

contractDivergences.contract: 'the search field on the dais at the arc's base'
contractDivergences.built: Built: GlobalSearch centered (max 36rem) beneath the hall, above the legend's end.

contractDivergences.contract: 'Every figure carries its source and date'
contractDivergences.built: Built for the leaderboards, most-active and latest-votes (as <caption>); the curated 'controversial laws' block carries per-item Source links but no date line, and the 'now' column carries a last-sync line.

components.name: The Seat (signature)
components.description: The atomic component of the hall: a circle in coalition blue. Filled = sitting member, hollow = misses the most votes, lit = the faction hovered or focused in the legend (in its own colour), dimmed = another faction is lit. Both blocs share one blue; the aisle carries the split, with the counts in the display face. Seats are pointer targets (tabindex -1); the legend is the keyboard path.

narrative.overview:
The whole site is the Knesset hall, seen live and drawn in the flag's own materials. The chrome is the flag's blue field with its two stripes ruled beneath it; the page is the warm cream of the building's Jerusalem-stone cladding; records sit on white paper separated from the stone by a hairline, never by a shadow. National symbols — the blue, the flag, the building — are how the site says "for everyone": no faction's colour is ever the page's colour. Coalition and opposition are the same blue, split by the aisle. The atomic component is the seat: a filled circle is a sitting member, a hollow one a member who misses votes; state lives in form and position, not in hue.

The register is civic and documentary — not editorial, not campaign, not playful. Frank Ruhl Libre, the face of the state's own documents, speaks only where the state speaks: the wordmark, the page title, the numerals at the aisle, and the one figure a finding leads with. Everything else is Heebo at a working size, dense enough for a record and calm enough to trust on a phone. Time-ranked findings are ruled rows and tables, never card grids, and every figure block ends with where its numbers came from and when.

Four scripts share one identity. Nothing in the system depends on uppercase, letter-spacing or a physical left and right: prominence comes from size, weight and ink; layout uses logical properties throughout; the hall itself is the one deliberate exception, fixed left-to-right like every election-night broadcast. Every token is defined under three roots — light, dark, and the high-contrast accessibility mode — and a test fails the build when a text/surface pair drops under WCAG AA in any of them.
keyCharacteristics: Flag blue on Jerusalem stone; white paper for records; ink for text.
One accent, one hue for both blocs; the aisle carries the split.
Hairline separation everywhere; elevation only for things that float.
The display serif for the state's voice only; Heebo for the working record.
Ruled rows and tables for anything ranked in time; source and date beneath every figure.
Logical direction, no uppercase, no tracking: finished in Hebrew, Arabic, Russian and English alike.
Three theme roots guarded by tests; the accessibility layer is a constraint the world respects.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The chrome is the flag's blue field and the accent is the same blue; no other saturated colour is ever a page's colour. Party colours from the factions data appear only where a faction is the subject — the legend swatch, and the seats lit while that faction is hovered or focused — never as decoration.

rules.name: The Aisle Rule
rules.body: Coalition and opposition are both Israel: `coalition` and `opposition` are the same blue in every root. The split is expressed by position — the aisle, a gap, a side — and by form, never by blue-versus-red.

rules.name: The Fill/Ink Rule
rules.body: `accent` is a fill and `accent-ink` is text, even though they are identical in light mode; in dark mode the fill (#3a6fd0) and the ink (#7db1f7) diverge, and code that used the fill as text goes illegible. The same holds for every status tone: `-soft` for a fill, `-ink` for its text.

rules.name: The Three Roots Rule
rules.body: Every colour token is declared under `:root`, `html.dark` and `html.a11y-contrast`, and `tests/qa/design-tokens.test.ts` fails the build if one is missing, if a text/surface pair drops under 4.5:1 (3:1 for the accent as a component and for the focus ring), or if a class in `src/` names a token that does not exist. Adding a colour means adding it three times.

rules.name: The State's Voice Rule
rules.body: Frank Ruhl Libre appears in exactly four places: the wordmark, the page title, the aisle numerals, and the leading figure of a finding. Section headings, labels and body stay in Heebo. A page that sets its h2s in the serif is speaking in the wrong voice.

rules.name: The Four Scripts Rule
rules.body: No `uppercase`, no `tracking-*`. Uppercase is a no-op in Hebrew and Arabic, and letter-spacing breaks Arabic cursive joining. A heading or label earns prominence from size, weight and `muted` ink only.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that sits in a column, in a row of figures, or beside another number is set `tabular-nums`, so rows do not jitter and columns align.

rules.name: The Ruled Rows Rule
rules.body: Anything ranked or ordered in time — a leaderboard, the latest votes, this week's sittings — is a ruled list or a table, never a grid of cards. A card is for one entity at a time (a member, a vote) or for a form.

rules.name: The Source Margin Rule
rules.body: Every block of figures ends with a caption line in `muted` naming its source and the date of the data it shows; a table carries it as its `<caption>`. A curated claim carries its own "Source" link in the margin beside it. A number without its source is not finished.

rules.name: The Logical Direction Rule
rules.body: Use logical properties and utilities only. The hall is the one deliberate exception, fixed left-to-right in every locale — opposition on the left of the aisle, coalition on the right — because that is the orientation of every election-night broadcast; the spectrum bar is the other, for the same reason.

rules.name: The Float-Only Rule
rules.body: `shadow-float` is for menus and panels — things that are not in the page's flow. Cards, tables, the search dais and the header never carry a shadow; if something needs separating, give it a hairline.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: card (0.75rem) > control (0.5rem) > chip (0.375rem); pills only for stateful tokens. Use the token utilities `rounded-card`, `rounded-control`, `rounded-chip` and `rounded-full`, never Tailwind's `rounded-lg`/`rounded-md` by name.

dos: Do use `bg-accent` for fills and `text-accent-ink` for text, and `bg-<tone>-soft` with `text-<tone>-ink` for badges; declare any new colour under all three roots.
Do separate a card from the page with `border border-line` on `bg-surface`, and reserve `shadow-float` for menus and panels.
Do set ranked or time-ordered data as ruled rows (`divide-y divide-line`) or a table inside `TableFrame`, and end every figure block with its source and date in caption `muted`.
Do set the page title, the wordmark, the aisle numerals and a finding's leading figure in `font-display`; keep everything else in Heebo.

Do set every number in a row or column `tabular-nums`, and wrap untranslated Hebrew in `dir="rtl" lang="he"` via `rtlAttrs` or `localizedAttrs`; give a run that opposes the page direction `text-end` as well.
Do use logical utilities (`ms-`, `pe-`, `border-s`, `text-start`, `end-0`) and the radius tokens (`rounded-card`, `rounded-control`, `rounded-chip`).
Do keep coalition and opposition in the same blue and express the split by the aisle, a gap, or a side.
Do make every interactive thing reachable by keyboard through a real link or button with a name; when a drawing has too many targets, provide a legend or list as the keyboard path.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated colour as decoration, or colour a bloc red; party colours are data and appear only where a faction is the subject.
Don't use `uppercase` or `tracking-*` anywhere, in any script.
Don't put a shadow on a card, a table, the search dais or the header.
Don't use raw Tailwind palette hues (`bg-green-100`, `text-amber-800`), `bg-white`, `bg-black/5` or `text-[11px]` in new code; the legacy ratchet lets no file add any.
Don't use physical left/right utilities, style props or declarations; the spectrum bar is the only allow-listed file.
Don't render a photograph as a hero, or lay statistics over an image of the building.
Don't open a page with a card grid of findings; a card is for one entity or one form.
Don't rely on hue alone for any state — a seat is hollow, a badge has a word, a result has a word.
